principle: Every check below is answered by reopening the produced file and looking. None is answered by reading what the agent said about it.

reuses.rust: src-tauri/src/agent_runtime/artifacts.rs::check — check_document, check_deck, check_workbook and the PDF reader already exist and already refuse an artifact that does not reopen. These checks extend that, they do not replace it.
reuses.python: An independent reopen with python-docx / python-pptx / openpyxl, so the file is judged by something other than the code that wrote it.

checks.check: The file parses as OOXML and word/document.xml is present.
checks.fails_when: The producer wrote a ZIP with the right extension and the wrong parts.

checks.check: Paragraph text contains the vessel tag, the inspection date, the governing measurement, the applicable minimum, a percentage, a date in YYYY-MM-DD form, and a signature line.
checks.fails_when: The document opens and says nothing the brief asked for.

checks.check: The text names which SOP revision the minimum came from.
checks.fails_when: A minimum allowable thickness appears with no revision beside it, which is the ambiguity the two-revision corpus exists to create.

checks.check: The text does not assert an internal inspection was performed or describe observed internal surface condition.
checks.fails_when: The note describes something the source explicitly says did not happen.

checks.check: The file parses as a presentation and reports its slide count.
Each slide has non-empty title text.
checks.fails_when: A deck renders as four blank rectangles and the producer calls it four slides.

checks.check: No slide asserts a remaining-life figure.
checks.fails_when: The deck states a number the inspection report explicitly declines to give.

checks.check: The file parses as a workbook and both named sheets exist.
The Assessment sheet's governing, wall-loss and below-minimum cells hold formulas, read with openpyxl data_only=False.
checks.fails_when: The cells hold the right constants. Right once, wrong the first time a reading changes.
checks.note: Rust's check_workbook already counts live formulas; this check reads the same property with a different library so agreement means something.

checks.check: Changing Readings!B4 from 8.2 to 9.3 and recalculating changes the governing value and the wall-loss percentage.
checks.blocked_when: No engine is available on this machine. Reported BLOCKED with the unblock command, never PASSED.
checks.unblock_command: Install LibreOffice and put soffice on PATH, then re-run with --recalc.

checks.check: Every citation the result carries names a document sha-256 that is in the fixture manifest and a page that exists in it.
checks.fails_when: A citation names a document that is not in the corpus, which is a fabricated source.

checks.check: Every published memory item claiming Provenance::ToolReceipt names an event_seq greater than zero that resolves to a recorded, successful event in the run's event log.
checks.fails_when: event_seq is 0 — see plan §3 finding 2 and src-tauri/src/subagents/worker.rs:391, which is the current state of this path.
checks.expected_result_today: FAIL, and that is the correct baseline reading. P02 is where it changes.

checks.check: The result carries a sha-256 of the produced file, and that hash matches the bytes on disk.
checks.fails_when: The recorded hash and the file disagree, which means the file changed after it was reported.

matching_rule: expected_any_of and forbidden_any_of are case-insensitive plain substrings, not regular expressions. This file is read by Node, Rust and Python, and one escaping convention per language is three chances to get it wrong.
